name: Half Butterfly to Leg Entanglements
keyCorrections: If they flatten your hook, you're too flat on your back — sit up on your far elbow.
If they step back and avoid the hook, extend into K-guard immediately — don't chase the hook.
If they drive forward into you, use their momentum for the bear trap entry.
description: Use the half butterfly hook to off-balance the opponent, then transition into K-guard, bear trap, or saddle when they react to the hook pressure.
shortInstruction: Half butterfly hook, off-balance, follow their reaction into leg entanglement or sweep.
summary: Half butterfly is the strongest transitional guard in modern no-gi. With one hook on their near leg and the other leg framing on their hip, you can off-balance them forward or sideways. Their reaction determines your entry: if they stand, go to K-guard; if they step back, enter bear trap; if they post, enter the saddle. The half butterfly is the engine that powers the entire lower-body attack system.
whyItWorks: The half butterfly hook on one leg gives you control over their base while keeping your other leg free to frame or attack.
It works against both standing and kneeling passers, making it one of the most versatile guard entries.
The half butterfly creates a dilemma: if they drive forward, they feed the sweep; if they posture out, they feed the leg entanglement.
Danaher/Heel Hook philosophy: half butterfly is the entry that solves the problem of 'how to get to the legs from guard.'
commonMistakes: Letting the half butterfly hook get flattened or stripped — the hook must stay active at all times.
Framing with the free leg on their hip instead of their biceps — hip frame gives space, biceps frame gives control.
Stopping at the half butterfly instead of flowing to the next position — half butterfly is transitional, not final.
Using the hook to lift instead of to off-balance — lift them = they post; off-balance them = they fall.
coachingCues: Hook active, free leg framing, feel the reaction.
Off-balance first, then enter — never skip the setup.
Half butterfly is the door — K-guard and saddle are the rooms.
If they stand, go K-guard. If they kneel, go bear trap.
safetySummary: Keep your head off the mat when off-balancing — protect your neck from guillotine counters.
Do not fully extend your legs into leg entanglements without controlling their hip — they can kick free and counter.
When transitioning to saddle, keep your foot on the outside of their leg to avoid reaping penalties.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Half butterfly hook on near leg: free leg frames on hip/biceps → off-balance forward or sideways → read their reaction → enter K-guard, bear trap, or saddle.

decisionTree.action: They stand → K-guard entry → backside or leg entanglement.
They drive forward → bear trap entry → sweep or leg lock.
They step back → saddle entry → heel hook.

moneyDetails: Your half butterfly hook should be deep — foot hooking behind their thigh, not just behind the knee.
Use your free leg to frame on their far hip, not their near hip — this controls their rotation.
Off-balance them by pulling your hook toward your own chest while pushing with the free leg frame.
The transition to K-guard is a single movement: extend the butterfly hook and rotate your hips 90 degrees.
nextStep: After half butterfly entries, learn K-guard and bear trap systems to chain with your leg entanglement attacks.
fixItFast: Hook flattened? Sit up on your elbow and pummel the hook back in.
They keep stepping back? Stop chasing — enter K-guard immediately.
They drive through you? Accept the pressure and enter bear trap — use their momentum against them.
